page_hint: Section 3, sensitivity dimensions list, final paragraph
quoted_clause: the same ~6.2–10.4M range reported with Fig 16.1 and in §16.6
observed: §16.6 (Architecture Consequence) discusses the ~7.5M point-estimate break-even but does not report the full ~6.2–10.4M range. The range is derived and reported in §16.3 (the sensitivity dimensions list and the 'Reading the result' paragraph). Fig 16.1's caption does report the range.
evidence: Section 6 text: 'self-host wins only once volume passes the ~7.5M break-even' — mentions 7.5M only. Section 3 text: 'the honest output is a range (here ~6.2–10.4M req/mo)' and 'the low end is 6,232,677.2 … the high end is 10,387,795.33' — reports the full range.
root_cause: Cross-reference points to the section discussing the point estimate rather than the section reporting the range.
correction: Change §16.6 to §16.3 (or to the specific subsection within §16.3 where the range is derived).
acceptance_test: The cross-reference resolves to a location that actually reports the ~6.2–10.4M range, not just the 7.5M point estimate.

page_hint: Section 3, Step 1 sizing table and surrounding prose
quoted_clause: Independent prefill screen — case (i) linear-only … case (iii) causal-triangle … case (ii) full-square conservative
observed: The three FLOP-counting cases (i), (ii), (iii) are used throughout the sizing table and surrounding prose but are not defined in this chapter. Descriptive labels ('linear-only,' 'causal-triangle,' 'full-square') hint at the mathematical basis but do not tell the reader what FLOPs are being counted or where the multipliers 1.0861 and 1.1723 come from.
evidence: The multipliers ×1.0861 and ×1.1723 appear without derivation. A reader who has not read the chapter where these cases are defined cannot verify the table or understand why the cases differ. The chapter references Ch 17 for fleet sizing but does not cross-reference the specific chapter/section defining the FLOP-counting cases.
root_cause: Concepts imported from another chapter without a cross-reference at the point of first use in this chapter.
correction: Add a brief parenthetical cross-reference at the first use: e.g., 'case (i) linear-only (defined in Ch __ §__)' or a one-sentence reminder: 'case (i) counts attention FLOPs linearly per token; case (ii) uses the full n² square; case (iii) uses the causal n²/2 triangle.'
acceptance_test: A reader encountering the sizing table for the first time can identify where the FLOP-counting cases and their multipliers are defined, either via cross-reference or a one-sentence in-chapter reminder.

quoted_clause: Two service times apply for the non-agentic canonical request (W ≈ 8.6 s: 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode), and, for the T=3 (95th-percentile) agentic request, the evaluator's 17.70 s under no prefix reuse and 14.16 s under 100% prefix reuse.
observed: The sentence structure grammatically attaches 'for the non-agentic canonical request' to 'Two service times apply,' reading as if there are two service times for the non-agentic case. In fact there is one non-agentic service time (8.6 s) and two agentic service times (17.70 s and 14.16 s), for three total. The parenthetical breaks 8.6 s into prefill and decode components, which are not separate service times.
evidence: The non-agentic case has a single W ≈ 8.6 s. The agentic case has two service times (17.70 s no-reuse, 14.16 s reuse). The sentence says 'Two service times apply for the non-agentic canonical request' which reads as two for the non-agentic case.
root_cause: Ambiguous sentence structure in the closing summary.
correction: Restructure: 'Three service times are used: W ≈ 8.6 s for the non-agentic canonical request (1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode), and for the T=3 agentic request, 17.70 s under no prefix reuse and 14.16 s under 100% prefix reuse.'
acceptance_test: A reader can count exactly three service times from the sentence without re-reading.

quoted_clause: the illustrative φ = 0.05 — halved from §17.6's φ = 0.1 to model a lower cross-host fraction at the grown 100-rps traffic
observed: The justification for halving φ from 0.1 to 0.05 is unclear. φ is defined as the fraction of requests requiring cross-host data; there is no stated mechanism by which higher traffic (100 rps vs 40 rps) would reduce this per-request fraction. The [ASSUMPTION] label is correct but the stated rationale does not follow from the variable's definition.
evidence: φ is defined in §17.4 as 'a fraction of requests require cross-host data.' Growing traffic from 40 to 100 rps does not inherently reduce the per-request probability of needing cross-host data unless the retrieval architecture changes, which is not stated.
root_cause: Unjustified assumption change presented with a rationale that does not follow from the variable's definition.
correction: Either provide a concrete mechanism (e.g., 'the retrieval service is also scaled, reducing the per-request cross-host fraction') or keep φ = 0.1 and note that B_min would be 50 MB/s = 0.40 Gbps, still well under the 10 Gbps link.
acceptance_test: The stated reason for φ changing is mechanically plausible given the variable's definition.

quoted_clause: The architect must choose between density (sticky sessions, higher per-host utilization) and evenness (stateless routing, lower per-host utilization but better load balance).
observed: The parenthetical claims sticky sessions give 'higher per-host utilization' and stateless routing gives 'lower per-host utilization.' This is not universally true: sticky sessions can create hot spots that reduce effective utilization (as the same paragraph acknowledges), and stateless routing does not inherently reduce per-host utilization unless context must be recomputed.
evidence: The same paragraph states 'a popular user can pin a single host to capacity while other hosts stand underutilized' — which contradicts the blanket claim of 'higher per-host utilization' for sticky sessions.
root_cause: Oversimplified trade-off framing that contradicts the paragraph's own earlier caveat.
correction: Rephrase: 'The architect must choose between state locality (sticky sessions, which keep conversation state on one host and avoid cross-host state transfer, but can create load imbalance if sessions are skewed) and load evenness (stateless routing, which distributes load evenly but may require recomputing context on each host).' Remove the blanket utilization claims or qualify them.
acceptance_test: The trade-off statement does not contradict the hot-spot caveat in the same paragraph.

quoted_clause: (entire reconciliation box — begins 'the four throughput rates in this book are different quantities')
observed: The reconciliation box is approximately one page of dense continuous prose mixing four distinct tasks: (1) defining four throughput rates, (2) decomposing the 2.0 req/s into prefill/decode components, (3) warning against summing rates across phases, and (4) suggesting a cost/phase-equivalence model. No internal structure (no numbered list, no table, no sub-headings) makes it likely readers will skim or skip it.
evidence: The box contains ~400 words of continuous prose with no structural breaks.
root_cause: Multiple distinct intellectual tasks compressed into a single unstructured callout.
correction: Break into: (a) a small table with four rows (rate, scope, phase, label), (b) a short prose warning about not summing rates, (c) move the phase-decomposition and cost-model discussion to a separate subsection or footnote.
acceptance_test: A reader can identify the four rates and their scopes within 30 seconds of looking at the box.

quoted_clause: (entire figure caption — begins 'Sizing a fleet by burst peak, headroom and failover')
observed: The figure caption is a paragraph-length block containing: figure description, scope note, burst profile note, ρ break-even calculation (ρ ≈ 0.917), cross-references to Chs. 17-20 and Ch 14, and evidence labels. This exceeds what a caption should carry.
evidence: The caption contains ~200 words including a numerical calculation and multiple cross-references.
root_cause: Caveats and calculations that belong in surrounding prose or a footnote are packed into the caption.
correction: Reduce caption to 2-3 sentences stating what the figure shows and its key scope limitation (ideal ρ=1 analytical ceiling, no SLO claim). Move the break-even calculation, burst profile note, and cross-references to the surrounding prose or a footnote.
acceptance_test: Caption is ≤3 sentences; break-even calculation appears in prose.

quoted_clause: the 21/31/32 host counts derived from that rate are therefore lower bounds: the check pushes the real count upward — by at least the ~7% headroom deficit under case (i)
observed: The conclusion that headline counts are lower bounds is important but the text does not provide corrected host counts. It states the direction ('upward') and approximate magnitude ('~7%') but leaves the reader without a concrete corrected number. An architect who reads only the headline counts could under-size.
evidence: Under case (i), if prefill uses 93% of the ceiling, the sustainable rate is ~1.86 req/s instead of ~2.0, giving N ≈ ⌈344/(1.86×17)⌉ ≈ 23 hosts at full utilization instead of 21. The text does not compute this.
root_cause: Analysis identifies the constraint but stops short of quantifying its effect on the headline numbers.
correction: Add one sentence: 'Under case (i), the prefill-constrained rate is ~1.86 req/s, requiring ~23 hosts at full utilization instead of 21; under cases (ii)/(iii) the prefill screen already binds and the counts in Table 17-1's prefill rows apply.'
acceptance_test: The paragraph provides at least one corrected host count that accounts for the prefill constraint.

quoted_clause: If sessions are stateless (the model is reloaded or KV cache is discarded between requests)
observed: 'The model is reloaded' is ambiguous. It could be misread as 'model weights are reloaded from disk,' which is not the intended meaning. The intended meaning is that each request starts with fresh context.
evidence: In context, the parenthetical explains what 'stateless' means: no carried-over conversation state. 'The model is reloaded' does not convey this.
root_cause: Imprecise phrasing in a parenthetical definition.
correction: Replace with: 'If sessions are stateless (each request starts with fresh context — no carried-over conversation state or KV cache), any host can serve any request.'
acceptance_test: A reader cannot reasonably interpret 'the model is reloaded' as weight reloading.

quoted_clause: ≈ 10 s planning round for the canonical non-agentic round
observed: The W_e2e ≈ 10 s value is stated without derivation or cross-reference in this chapter. The table simultaneously states W_queue is 'unmeasured here,' creating tension: if W_e2e = 10 s and W_GPU-exec = 8.6 s, then W_queue ≈ 1.4 s is derivable.
evidence: No citation or cross-reference accompanies the 10 s value. The W_queue row says 'unmeasured here.'
root_cause: Provenance gap for a specific numerical value used in a comparison table.
correction: Add a cross-reference (e.g., 'Ch 4, Table 4-2') or note that 10 s is an illustrative planning value including network/LB overhead beyond queue + GPU execution.
acceptance_test: The 10 s value has a stated source or is explicitly labeled as illustrative.

observed: Uses 24.1 GB (KV at initial 9,200-token residency) while the chapter's canonical per-request KV at max context (9,500 tokens) is 24.9 GB. During decode, KV grows from 24.1 to 24.9 GB, so the average is ~24.5 GB.
evidence: 9,200 × 2.62 MB = 24.1 GB (initial); 9,500 × 2.62 MB = 24.9 GB (max). The calculation uses 24.1 without explanation.
root_cause: Inconsistent KV residency value between the initial-residency figure and the max-context figure used elsewhere in the chapter.
correction: Either use 24.9 GB (max context, consistent with the chapter's C calculation) or add a parenthetical: '(24.1 GB at initial 9,200-token residency; 24.9 GB at max 9,500-token context — the conclusion ≈14× holds either way).'
acceptance_test: The KV value used in the decode-leg calculation is either consistent with the chapter's canonical 24.9 GB or explicitly justified as the initial-residency value.

observed: 200 × 17.70 = 3,540, not 3,541. The table header states W=17.70 s but the actual evaluator value is 17.703... s, giving 200 × 17.703 = 3,540.6 → 3,541. The stated W and the computed value are inconsistent by 1 unit.
root_cause: Rounding of W to 17.70 in the header while the computation uses the unrounded value.
correction: Either state W as ≈17.70 s with a note that the table uses the unrounded evaluator value, or change 3,541 to 3,540.
acceptance_test: 200 × (stated W) rounds to the value in the table.

quoted_clause: typically ρ ∈ [0.95, 0.98] depending on LB sophistication
observed: The ρ range is stated in §17.2 without an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] label, while §17.4 explicitly labels the same values as '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] engineering thresholds, not universal vendor-independent constants.'
evidence: §17.2 has no label; §17.4 has the label for the same values.
root_cause: Evidence-label inconsistency between the mental model introduction and the detailed treatment.
correction: Add [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] in §17.2 or add a forward reference: '(see §17.4 for scope and labeling).'
acceptance_test: The ρ range carries the same evidence label in both §17.2 and §17.4.

observed: The '/' separator is ambiguous — it could be read as a fraction (94 + 1/75 + 1) rather than two separate values (94+1=95 and 75+1=76).
evidence: Context indicates two separate u-only variants: 95 (no-reuse) and 76 (reuse). The '/' notation does not clearly convey this.
root_cause: Ambiguous mathematical notation for two parallel values.
correction: Write 'the u-only variants read 95 and 76 (94+1 and 75+1)' or use 'and' instead of '/'.
acceptance_test: A reader can identify two distinct values without ambiguity.

page_hint: §17.7 What We Still Don't Know, third bullet
quoted_clause: The cost of adding a host is roughly the cost of 8×H100 (multi-hundred-thousand dollars).
observed: Time-sensitive cost estimate without a date or scope qualifier. Hardware prices change across generations and market conditions.
evidence: No date, price source, or scope (list vs. street vs. cloud) accompanies the estimate.
root_cause: Undated cost claim in a rapidly changing market.
correction: Add a date and scope: e.g., 'roughly the cost of 8×H100 (multi-hundred-thousand dollars at 2026 list prices)' or reframe around the mechanism: 'the capital cost of one 8-GPU host.'
acceptance_test: The cost estimate carries a date or is reframed to avoid time-sensitivity.

quoted_clause: kernel time-slicing between concurrent GPU kernels
observed: 'Kernel time-slicing' is not standard terminology for GPU kernel contention. GPUs share SM resources among concurrent kernels through spatial partitioning (block scheduling), not temporal time-slicing in the CPU sense. The term could mislead readers into imagining a round-robin temporal schedule.
evidence: NVIDIA GPU concurrent kernel execution shares SM resources via block-level scheduling; 'time-slicing' is associated with MPS process scheduling, not intra-kernel contention.
root_cause: Imprecise hardware terminology.
correction: Replace with 'SM resource contention between concurrent kernels' or 'interference from concurrent kernel launches.'
acceptance_test: The mechanism named matches NVIDIA's documented concurrent-kernel execution model.

quoted_clause: if stateless, use least-connections or power-of-two-choices so load follows capacity — do not use consistent hashing.
observed: 'Do not use consistent hashing' is too strong. Consistent hashing provides reasonable load distribution for stateless routing; its weakness is that it distributes based on request key rather than actual load, which can create imbalance when request costs vary. The advice is directionally correct but the absolute prohibition is not justified.
evidence: Consistent hashing is widely used for stateless load balancing (e.g., in CDN and API gateway configurations). Its limitation is load-adaptivity, not correctness.
root_cause: Overly prescriptive advice without stated mechanism.
correction: Replace with: 'consistent hashing distributes based on request key rather than actual load, so it can create imbalance when request costs vary; prefer least-connections or power-of-two-choices, which adapt to actual load.'
acceptance_test: The advice states the mechanism behind the recommendation rather than an absolute prohibition.

page_hint: §17.7 What We Still Don't Know, fifth bullet
quoted_clause: which are not yet well understood
observed: 'Not yet well understood' is vague. Single-host prefix caching is well-understood (implemented in vLLM, SGLang). The genuine unknown is cross-host cache hit-rate distribution and lookup latency under realistic multi-host traffic.
evidence: The sentence refers to 'cross-host cache-invalidation protocols for that prefix/retrieval cache' but does not specify what aspect is unknown.
root_cause: Vague uncertainty statement that could be read as 'the whole area is unknown' rather than 'specific measurements are missing.'
correction: Specify: 'the hit-rate distribution across hosts under realistic traffic, and the latency cost of cross-host cache lookup, are not well characterized for multi-host deployments.'
acceptance_test: The uncertainty is specific enough to suggest what measurement would resolve it.

quoted_clause: For N = 4 in the no-spare case (no N−1 reserve held back), a single-host loss reduces capacity from 100% to 75% ... under the chapter's N−1 spare model (31 working → 32 total) one loss is absorbed without touching serving capacity.
observed: The paragraph mixes two different fleet scenarios (N=4 from the figure/burst scenario and N=31/32 from the canonical scenario) without clearly separating them, which could confuse readers about which scenario the failover analysis applies to.
evidence: N=4 comes from Fig 17.1's burst-sizing example; N=31/32 comes from the canonical 40-rps peak sizing. They appear in the same paragraph.
root_cause: Two distinct scenarios discussed in one paragraph without visual or structural separation.
correction: Separate into two sentences or a brief list: '(a) In the figure's 4-host burst scenario, no-spare: 3/4 = 75% residual. (b) In the canonical 31-working/32-total scenario: one loss is absorbed by the spare.'
acceptance_test: Each failover example is clearly associated with its fleet scenario.

observed: The dedicated-placement host count '32 with policy' is not reproducible from the stated methodology. Applying the 70%×95% derate to per-tier concurrency — the method used for the shared-pool calculation '⌈344/(9 × 0.665)⌉ = 58' in the same paragraph — yields 19 + 6 + 4 = 29 hosts, not 32. The value 32 is only reachable by applying the derate to the host count after ceiling instead (⌈13/0.665⌉ + ⌈4/0.665⌉ + ⌈3/0.665⌉ = 20 + 7 + 5 = 32), which is a different methodology than the shared-pool formula used one sentence earlier.
evidence: Shared pool (derate C): ⌈344/(9×0.665)⌉ = ⌈57.48⌉ = 58. Dedicated with same method: 8-bit ⌈240.8/(20×0.665)⌉ = ⌈18.10⌉ = 19; MoE ⌈68.8/(20×0.665)⌉ = ⌈5.17⌉ = 6; FP16 ⌈34.4/(17×0.665)⌉ = ⌈3.04⌉ = 4; total = 29. The printed 32 requires derate-N (derate applied to host count after ceiling), which is inconsistent with the shared-pool '58 with policy' calculation in the same paragraph.
root_cause: Inconsistent derate methodology between shared-pool and dedicated-placement calculations, or a numerical error in the dedicated-placement total.
correction: Either (a) recompute dedicated placement using the same derate-C method as the shared pool and print 29, or (b) explicitly state that dedicated placement uses a different derate method (derate applied to host count) and explain why the two methods differ, or (c) if 32 includes per-tier spares, show the spare calculation explicitly.
acceptance_test: The reader can reproduce the printed '32 with policy' from the stated inputs using a single, explicitly stated derate methodology that is consistent with the shared-pool '58 with policy' calculation in the same paragraph.
